entries.clue: Something for a religious arse steeped in drink to heave (4,2)

a church bench for a churchgoer to sit on

annotation.surface: A drunken churchgoer about to be sick.
annotation.walkthrough: The religious arse is a churchgoer's backside, and a pew is what it sits on. Heave here is to retch.
annotation.definitionFit: Heave is a plain synonym in its sense of retching, and spew up is the coarse phrasal verb for being sick.

entries.clue: Satisfy yourself young Mister Harry is to be heard (10)

indicators.note: the pieces are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: Master is the title for a young boy; to bait is to harry

annotation.surface: A command to please yourself, then a boy called Harry wanting to be listened to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Master' is the old-fashioned title for a boy, the young Mister; harry is a verb here, to harass, which is to bait.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: satisfying yourself stands for sexual self-pleasure, the plain sense of the answer.

entries.clue: Labour starts from here – true bastard American (6)

blocks.note: anagram fodder
US = American

annotation.surface: A political jibe about where the Labour Party begins, calling someone an American bastard.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour is childbirth, not the political party: contractions start in the uterus.
annotation.definitionFit: The uterus is the womb, where the labour of childbirth begins.

entries.clue: (& 25dn.) Miliband, ultimately hollow, is packaged by whippersnapper as a big star (4)

last letter of Miliband
a pit is a hollow

annotation.surface: Ed Miliband, empty at the core, being marketed by a young upstart as a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 4 down and 25 down. Hollow looks like it describes Miliband, but it is the noun, a pit.

entries.clue: On your back, scrubbing tip of todger? That should help with semen production (8)

definitions.text: That should help with semen production

indicators.note: a letter is scrubbed out of the word

should name the letter scrubbed, but the tip of todger is T while the letter actually removed from PROSTRATE is R

annotation.surface: Someone lying back and cleaning the end of their penis.
annotation.walkthrough: PROSTRATE and PROSTATE are often confused. The parse only works by removing R, while 'tip of todger' points to T, so the clue appears to contain a slip. A todger is British slang for a penis.
annotation.definitionFit: The prostate gland produces fluid that forms part of semen.

entries.clue: (& 24dn.) You'll be in grave trouble being so straight – mate indiscriminately! (4)

indicators.note: without order, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: as in 'dead straight'
MATE rearranged

annotation.surface: A warning that being too straight-laced will ruin you, so sleep around.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 6 down and 24 down. The definition is a pun: dead meat is in trouble, and the dead are in graves.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who is dead meat is in serious trouble; the grave pun fits the dead.

entries.clue: Balls gets not much applause, having coarse mouth (8)

blocks.note: a single clap is scant applause
trap is coarse slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

annotation.surface: Someone called Balls gets a feeble response for being foul-mouthed.
annotation.walkthrough: Balls looks like Ed Balls, the Labour politician, but it is the slang for nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Balls is slang for nonsense, which is claptrap.

entries.clue: Players pissed round toilet's entrance – it took some pluck in the old days (8)

definitions.text: it took some pluck in the old days

the anagrammed letters go round the T

blocks.note: anagram fodder, arranged around the T
first letter of toilet

annotation.surface: A band of drunken musicians gathered round the lavatory door.
annotation.walkthrough: The pluck is literal: a psaltery was a medieval stringed instrument played by plucking, so the definition is a cryptic hint rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an old plucked stringed instrument, so it took some plucking in the old days.

entries.clue: Tory no. 2 teamed with pisspoor, energy-lacking leader – nightmare! (6)

indicators.note: take the second letter of Tory
a badly done version of the word, so its letters are jumbled
remove E, the symbol for energy

blocks.note: second letter of Tory
LEADER minus one E (energy) leaves LADER, rearranged to RDEAL

annotation.surface: A jibe that a Tory deputy paired with a feeble, listless leader would be a nightmare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teamed with' only puts the two pieces side by side. The anagram works on LADER, the five letters left once one E is gone.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: a nightmare is any dreadful experience, and an ordeal is the painful trial one has to live through.

entries.clue: About Rev. Blair's capital cash dispenser: one inside's reported with no change (8)

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, as in about-turn, so REV faces the other way
a capital letter is the one at the start, so the first letter of Blair

first letter of Blair
automated teller machine, holding I
I = one, placed inside ATM

annotation.surface: Tony Blair's money machine, with someone on the inside, being reported unchanged.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rev. Blair jokes at Tony Blair's piety. Verbatim reports words exactly, with no change.
annotation.definitionFit: Verbatim means repeated word for word, reported with no change.

entries.clue: John leaves the battle site – wet! (5)

blocks.note: Waterloo, where Napoleon was defeated in 1815
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo; removed from WATERLOO

annotation.surface: Someone named John walking off a famous battlefield in the rain.
annotation.walkthrough: John looks like a man's name but is the slang word for a toilet. A loo is the British word for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Wet can be a noun for rain or liquid, which is water.

anagram fodder, 8 letters, following the D

annotation.surface: Spin doctors covering up a blunder by Ed Miliband.
annotation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party from 2010 to 2015. 'Put a spin on' is a past participle phrase like 'dressed up', in the sense of presenting something flatteringly.
annotation.definitionFit: To dress something up is to present it more attractively than it deserves, which is putting a spin on it.

entries.clue: Pervy as a prole on getting end away producing UV protection device (7)

blocks.note: PROLE loses its final E, leaving ASAPROL to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A lecherous working-class man having sex, with a smutty double meaning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply removes the last letter of prole. A prole is a working-class person.
annotation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, which protects against ultraviolet rays.

entries.clue: Monument? Come down to earth, Thatcher! (8)

blocks.note: to land is to come down to the ground
Mark Thatcher, son of Margaret Thatcher

annotation.surface: A call for Mrs Thatcher to be realistic about her own monument.
annotation.walkthrough: Thatcher looks like Margaret, the former prime minister, but it is her son Mark. The question mark makes the definition tentative.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a monument is one kind of landmark, a conspicuous structure people navigate by or visit.

entries.clue: Blair broadcast dropped by summer – which peer takes the piss out of (7)

definitions.text: which peer takes the piss out of

indicators.note: the AIR is dropped from BLAIR

blocks.note: BLAIR minus AIR (broadcast, as in to air a programme)
a summer is one who adds up, an adder; 'by' puts it beside BL

annotation.surface: Tony Blair's broadcasts, cancelled by a summer, being mocked by a lord.
annotation.walkthrough: A peer is a member of the House of Lords, but here it is one who pees. Summer, as in one who sums, gives ADDER.
annotation.definitionFit: The bladder is the organ a person who pees empties, taking urine out of it.

entries.clue: Howe, leader-wise in awful dread yet, departs (the "wet" having been got rid of) (10)

indicators.note: in the manner of a leader, meaning only the letter at the front of Howe
a mess, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of Howe
anagram fodder
d = departs, as on timetables

annotation.surface: Geoffrey Howe fearfully quitting, the 'wets' having been purged.
annotation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was a Thatcher-era minister, and the 'wets' were her moderate Tory opponents. Here the wet is simply water, removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Something dehydrated has had its water, the wet, removed.

entries.clue: Very speedy article by Nick leads to arse-kicking (8,3,4)

blocks.note: as in 'a cracking pace'
the definite article
to nick and to whip are both British slang for steal

annotation.surface: A fast piece of writing by someone named Nick prompting a good kicking.
annotation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a name but is British slang for steal, as is whip. Cracking the whip is making people work hard, as a verb-phrase noun matching arse-kicking.
annotation.definitionFit: Cracking the whip means imposing strict discipline, which is what arse-kicking means figuratively.

entries.clue: Bring some culture to Channel Islands Elvis impersonator, initially crap (8)

indicators.note: take the first letter of impersonator
badly made, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: abbreviation for the Channel Islands
ELVIS plus I, the first letter of impersonator, rearranged

annotation.surface: Bringing refinement to the Channel Islands through a terrible Elvis tribute act.
annotation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey, lie off the French coast. 'Initially' belongs to impersonator only, giving the single I.
annotation.definitionFit: To civilise is to bring culture and refinement to a people or place.

entries.clue: Charity gives Brand head (8)

a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

annotation.surface: A charity awarding Russell Brand a leading role.
annotation.walkthrough: Brand looks like the comedian Russell Brand, but it means a kind. Ness is a headland in place names.
annotation.definitionFit: Charity in its older sense of love for others is a plain synonym, not the donation-collecting organisation the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Country's massive performer of hot blow job consumed by energy (7)

annotation.walkthrough: The 'blow job' is a volcano's eruption, not a sex act: Etna in Sicily is a massive volcano. The 's after Country is 'has', a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia.

entries.clue: see 6dn. (4)
